URL: https://www.reuters.com/world/china/us-sees-chinese-invasion-taiwan-unlikely-next-year-despite-2027-timeline-sources-2026-10-01/
Reuters EXCLUSIVE (Phil Stewart and Idrees Ali, Washington) — published 1 October 2026, 05:02 UTC (06:02 BST)

US officials believe a Chinese invasion of Taiwan before 2028 is increasingly unlikely despite Chinese President Xi Jinping's instructions for his military to be ready by 2027 to take the democratically governed island by force, if needed, people familiar with US thinking said.
Bullet points as published:
- US officials see Beijing more likely to consider force in 2028 and beyond.
- Sources cite PLA readiness delays amid Xi's anti-corruption campaign as a significant factor.
- Some Chinese officials hope Taiwan's 2028 vote yields a government more amenable to Beijing, sources say.
The main reasons include delays in military readiness amid the Chinese Communist Party's anti-corruption campaign as well as Beijing's eagerness to see the [outcome of Taiwan's 2028 election — sentence truncated in retrieved excerpt].

https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/chinese-refiners-suspend-oct-fuel-exports-petrochina-cancels-cargoes-sources-say-2026-10-01/ — Reuters, 1 Oct 2026 04:57 UTC. Chinese refiners have suspended exports of oil products to regions beyond Hong Kong and Macau until further notice from Beijing, four people briefed on the matter said on Thursday. State oil major PetroChina cancelled on Wednesday a handful of its gasoline and jet fuel shipments planned for October, three of the sources said. Zhejiang Petrochemical did not plan exports during the holiday week. Unclear if Beijing would permit exports after October 7. The suspension will further constrain global markets already grappling with the loss of supplies [from Iran/the Gulf — sentence truncated].
